subject: Maths
title: Direct proportion
subtitle: Proportion · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve problems involving direct proportion using the unitary method and formulae.

key_vocab.definition: Two quantities are in direct proportion if when one doubles, the other doubles too. Their ratio stays constant.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve problems involving direct proportion using the unitary method and formulae.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Direct proportion -- Two quantities are in direct proportion if when one doubles, the other doubles too. Their ratio stays constant.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
If y is directly proportional to x, then y = kx where k is the constant of proportionality.
y = k × x
k = y ÷ x (the constant ratio)

Key examples:
  ✓ If 3 pens cost £6, then 1 pen costs £2  (unitary method)
  ✓ y = kx means y is directly proportional to x  (formula)
  ✓ Doubling x doubles y in direct proportion  (constant ratio)
  ✗ If 3 pens cost £6, then 5 pens cost £8  (added 2 instead of using ratio)
  ✗ y = kx + c is direct proportion  (must pass through origin)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – unitary method
  5 books cost £35. Find the cost of 8 books.
  Cost of 1 book: 35 ÷ 5 = £7
  Cost of 8 books: 7 × 8
  = £56
  = £56
  (Find the cost of one first, then multiply.)

Example 2 – finding k
  y is directly proportional to x. When x = 4, y = 20. Find y when x = 7.
  y = kx, so k = 20 ÷ 4 = 5
  y = 5x
  When x = 7: y = 5 × 7 = 35
  y = 35
  (Find k first, write the formula, then substitute.)

sections.title: Unitary method
sections.content:
Find the value of one, then scale up.

(a) 3 pens cost £4.50. Cost of 7?
(b) 5 kg costs £12.50. Cost of 8 kg?
(c) 4 tickets cost £60. Cost of 10?
(d) 6 oranges cost £1.80. Cost of 9?

sections.title: Finding the constant
sections.content:
y is directly proportional to x. Find k and the missing value.

(a) x = 3, y = 12. Find y when x = 5
(b) x = 4, y = 28. Find y when x = 6
(c) x = 10, y = 45. Find x when y = 27
(d) x = 2, y = 9. Find y when x = 8

sections.title: Scaling recipes
sections.content:
Scale each ingredient.

(a) Recipe for 4: 200g flour. Amount for 10?
(b) Recipe for 6: 450ml milk. Amount for 4?
(c) Recipe for 8: 320g sugar. Amount for 5?
(d) Recipe for 3: 150g butter. Amount for 12?

sections.title: Direct proportion problems
sections.content:
Solve each proportion problem.

(a) A car uses 6 litres for 72 km. How far on 10 litres?
(b) 3 workers build a wall in 12 hours. How long for 1 worker?
(c) £1 = 1.15 euros. Convert £45 to euros.
(d) A map scale: 2 cm = 5 km. What is 7 cm in km?

sections.title: Mixed direct proportion
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) y ∝ x. x = 6, y = 18. Find y when x = 11
(b) y ∝ x². x = 2, y = 12. Find y when x = 5
(c) 8 identical books weigh 2.4 kg. Weight of 15?
(d) A journey of 150 miles takes 2.5 hours. Time for 210 miles?
(e) y ∝ √x. x = 9, y = 6. Find y when x = 25

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ Direct proportion means y = kx
✗ In direct proportion, as x increases y decreases
✓ The graph of direct proportion passes through the origin
✗ If 3 costs £6, then 5 costs £6 + £2 = £8
✓ k = y ÷ x is the constant of proportionality
